LESSON: READING 14.4.1 EXTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORY (CLASS READER)

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.4: Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story (Class Reader)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story (Class Reader), part of Strand 14 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: Where does a writer get what to write about? 2. How are stories related to what happens in real life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story (Class Reader) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Problem solving is inculcated as the learners make connections between the short stories and their own experiences.

• Communication and collaboration is achieved as the learner works in pairs or groups to undertake different tasks.

Values:
Social justice is enhanced as all learners with varied abilities dramatise and record sections of the short story that reflect real

life experiences.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Social cohesion is promoted as learners relate the text to real life experiences and make informed decisions in their lives.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:


Remember the key question: Where does a writer get what to write about? 2. How are stories related to what happens in real life?
